answer: Picture the honest agents as a garden where each plant is tended by many unrelated hands. To become established, a newcomer must collect vouches from graders whose own endorsement neighborhoods barely overlap, like a sparrow fed by flocks from far corners rather than one nest. A sybil ring's graders all perch on the same sable branch, so their mutual-overlap score spikes and the protocol discounts the whole cluster. Faking standing then means infiltrating many genuinely separate subcommunities: linear social cost per identity, not one cheap mint.
